description:
## Question

Survey real NIF code (Hex packages using Rustler/Zigler/elixir_make/C NIFs, GitHub, ElixirForum threads asking for 'a NIF for X') and group it into workload categories. For each: representative packages, input/output data shapes (binaries, lists, numbers, strings, maps), call pattern (one big call vs many small), whether it blocks schedulers or uses dirty schedulers, and why the author went native. Output: a ranked candidate list of target workloads with the evidence.

comments.text: Research findings: branch research/nif-workloads, docs/research/nif-workloads.md. Summary: Most NIFs on Hex (about 47 of the top 50 Rustler packages, plus bcrypt/argon2/vix/exqlite/explorer) wrap an existing library, and defk can't help there. The hand-written ones are a long tail, mostly loops over packed binaries, and many either block normal schedulers (evil_crc32c, bandit_native mask, Membrane mixer) or hand-roll chunking or dirty twins (ex_data_sketch, ecsv). Ranked targets: (1) byte transforms (WS masking, CRC32C, pixel conversion), (2) PCM audio mixing, (3) batched HLL/CMS sketch updates, (4) f32 vector distances/NMS, (5) batched string distance, (6) time-series encode/stats. Several have a pure-Elixir twin to use as the baseline (Bandit ws_mask, Membrane Adder, ExDataSketch.Backend.Pure). Main gaps: bitwise ops, [f32]/[i16]/[i32] types, wrapping u64 hash arithmetic.

Resolution: most NIFs wrap an existing library (about 47 of the top 50 Rustler packages; bcrypt, libvips, SQLite, Polars, XLA). defk can't help with these. Hand-written algorithms are a long tail of small packages, mostly loops over packed binaries, and many block normal schedulers with no size limit (evil_crc32c, Bandit's WS masking, Membrane's mixer, ex_strsim). The careful ones hand-roll scheduling (ex_data_sketch's dirty twin above 10k items, ecsv's chunking), which is what defk's automatic yielding replaces. Ranked candidates: 1 byte transforms (WS masking, CRC32C/16, pixel formats); 2 PCM audio mixing with clipping (Membrane has C and Elixir versions); 3 batched sketch updates (HLL, count-min, Bloom); 4 f32 vector kernels; 5 batched string distance; 6 time-series encoding and rolling stats. Not targets: persistent mutable data structures, parsers that build terms, library wrappers, tiny per-call math. Gaps: bitwise ops (defk-w38), [f32]/[i16]/[i32], opt-in wrapping u64 arithmetic for hashes. Detail: branch research/nif-workloads, docs/research/nif-workloads.md.
